did_you_know.text: The chapter opens with a description of Elijah’s ascent to heaven in a whirlwind, while also recounting the journey Elijah and Elisha took together from Gilgal.
Elijah asks Elisha to stay at Bethel, but Elisha swears that he will not leave him. This highlights Elisha’s loyalty and perseverance.
The sons of the prophets at Bethel know that Elijah is about to be taken away, and Elisha replies that he knows it too, asking them, “Be silent.”
Fifty of the sons of the prophets stand at a distance and watch Elijah and Elisha near the Jordan, but they do not cross the river with them.

Elijah strikes the water with his mantle, and the Jordan is divided in two. Elijah and Elisha cross on dry ground, resembling the miraculous crossings of bodies of water described elsewhere in the Bible.

Before his departure, Elijah offers Elisha the opportunity to ask for something, and Elisha requests, “Please let me have a double portion of your spirit.” The request is phrased as a plea for a double share of Elijah’s spirit.
A chariot of fire and horses of fire separate Elijah from Elisha, and Elijah ascends to heaven in a whirlwind. In this vision, fire is described as the means of separation and ascent.

After Elijah’s departure, Elisha takes his mantle, strikes the waters of the Jordan, and calls out, “Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?” The waters divide before him as well, and the sons of the prophets recognize that Elijah’s spirit rests on him.
The people of Jericho describe their city as a good place to live, but they explain that its water is bad and that the land causes death and miscarriage.

Elisha asks for a new bowl and some salt, and he throws the salt into the spring. He then declares in the name of the LORD that the water has been healed, and the text testifies that it remained healed to his day.
